doc.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Carole King's Jazzman: his woodwind battery and being told to play what he feels
summary: Called by Lou Adler, he brought his woodwinds and played tenor on Carole King's Jazzman.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: my previous trips into A&M. So I get a call, “Carole King would like you to play on her record.” Okay, great. What instruments do I need? I need a tenor saxophone, okay, great. Because at the time you know I regularly was expected to have at my fingertips well my woodwind battery consisted of piccolo, flute, alto flute, bass flute, clarinet, bass clarinet, soprano — actually sopranino, soprano, alto, tenor, baritone and then recorders. I had a soprano recorder, a tenor recorder — yeah those two. So it was a lot of horns there to deal with. It was — for any of us woodwind players it was a good idea to have a big trunk behind your car because you needed the storage space. Anyway so I go in with Carole King and they’re very sweet. They play me the tune and you know Lou Adler says, “Look just play what you feel.” Okay. And that happens often. “Play what you feel.”
Did you even ask like well what key is it in? Or do you just wait until you put the headphones on and you —
Yeah I found it pretty quickly what key it was in. Fortunately that one was in C, that one. So the people’s key.
Of course D for the tenor saxophone.
Yeah sometimes you get those things like they’re in the key of B and you’re thinking oh my licks, I don’t know if I can play those in C sharp.
